then.text: The brook's clear and the fish are back. There's an otter on the far bank right now, looking pleased with itself. You did that.
Otters were all but gone from most of England by the 1970s. Pesticides and dirty water did it. Now they are back in nearly every county. Let's keep it that way.
You've seen the outfall, the angler, the docks, the Director, the launderette and the culvert. That's the lot. Who is it?

Hazel Bell, otter warden. Volunteer, kettle-carrier, professional squinter at brooks.

Otters were all but gone from most of England by the 1970s. Pesticides and dirty rivers did it. They've crept back up the Mersey basin, and now something nasty is getting into the water here and the fish are floating.
It's being tipped in. I want to know who. There are three likely people: a loud Director, an angler, and a man with a van. I'll not say which is which.

Look at things, ask folk, write it down. Your Fieldbook has a Casebook tab now; press Run on the Fieldbook until you find it. When you're sure, come back and name them. A wrong name will cost you standing, and rightly.

then.text: Mavis Crabtree, secretary of the angling club, and I have never once left a fish in a worse state than I found it.
These waders? Green to the knee. I've been testing the brook for the club since March. Pondweed, mud, a very surprised newt. It is not a crime.
And I'll tell you something useful. The fish only turn up on Wednesdays. Whatever goes in, goes in on Tuesday evening, on the ebb, so the tide whisks it away.

else.text: Lovely brook, this. Mind the newts.

lighthouse_fan.text: That's Leasowe Lighthouse, built in 1763. The oldest brick-built lighthouse in Britain.
It shone out over the Mersey long before anyone had heard of satnav. Honestly, it's better than satnav.

tide_walker.text: Hilbre Island! You can walk out at low tide, two hours either side. Miss it and you wait for the next tide. Twelve hours.
There's a colony of grey seals out there. Hundreds. They pretend not to notice you.

cyclist.text: This path was the Hooton to West Kirby railway until 1962. Now it's twelve miles of flat, tree-lined cycling.
I do it every Sunday. I'd say it's relaxing if the geese would stop heckling.

icecream.text: Parkgate used to be a port. Ships sailed from here to Ireland. Then the River Dee silted up and left us a marsh.
Now we sell ice cream to people looking at where the sea used to be. It's good business.

seal_whisperer.text: Shh. Not so loud. You waded through the channel? Brave. Or silly. Possibly both.

then.text: The seals like you. That's all I'll say. They're very judgemental.

else.text: Here, take these. The seals insist. They don't know what a snare is, but they know a good bag when they see one.
